$comment: Every upstream selector this package's CSS depends on is recorded here,
grouped by the surface file it came from. tests/galata/selector-integrity.mjs
boots each supported JupyterLab build, drives each named state, and asserts
that every entry in `selectors` matches at least one element. A selector that
stops matching is an upstream markup change, and it must fail the build here
rather than surface later as a visual regression nobody can explain.
Entries are written WITHOUT the `body[data-jp-theme-name^='Data4Now']` scope
that every rule in the CSS carries — see `scope` below. The harness is
asserting that upstream still emits the element, not that our own rule is
present, so prefixing would only test the theme attribute over and over.
`optional: true` means the state exists in JupyterLab but is not reliably
reachable from a scripted boot (a disabled menu item, a dirty tab, a bad
regex). The harness should report those as skipped, never as passes, and
never fail the build on them.
`nonQueryable` records rules whose selector is a pseudo-element or a
pseudo-class that `querySelectorAll` cannot evaluate. They are listed for
completeness of the ownership record — §7.4(5) asks for every selector we
depend on, not only the assertable ones — and are not asserted.

states.boot: Cold start, default layout: left sidebar open on the file browser, launcher in the dock.
states.document-open: A notebook or text file open in the main dock area.
states.document-dirty: An open document with unsaved changes, so its tab shows the dirty dot.
states.dock-split: The dock area split at least once, so a dock handle exists.
states.menu-open: A top-level menu bar dropdown open (File).
states.menu-open-keyboard: A menu opened and then moved with ArrowDown, so an item carries .lm-mod-active.
states.menu-open-view: The View menu open, which is where the toggled items live.
states.context-menu-open: A context menu opened on a file browser row.
states.notebook-open: A notebook open with at least one code cell.
states.notebook-executed: A notebook with at least one executed cell that produced output.
states.notebook-error-output: A notebook cell executed to a traceback or a stderr stream.
states.dialog-open: Any modal dialog open (File ▸ Rename works).
states.dialog-warn-open: A dialog with a destructive confirmation button (kernel shutdown).
states.document-search-open: The Ctrl/Cmd-F overlay open over a document.
states.document-search-regex-error: The search overlay in regex mode with an unparseable pattern.
states.extension-manager-open: The extension manager panel open in the sidebar.
states.right-panel-open: The right sidebar open on the property inspector.
states.debugger-open: The debugger panel open, which is where the accordion titles are.
states.document-loading: A document mid-load, while its spinner is on screen.
states.running-panel-open: The Running Terminals and Kernels panel open in the left sidebar with at least one live kernel.
states.log-console-open: The Log Console open in the down area with at least one logged message.
states.bottom-dock-open: Any widget open in the '#jp-down-stack' down area, so its TabPanel tab bar and the vsplit handle exist.
states.toast-visible: A notification toast on screen. JupyterLab raises the Jupyter-news prompt on a first boot with a fresh profile, so this is reachable but not deterministic; the entries are optional until the harness can raise one on demand.

selectors.note: MenuBar moves this on pointer AND keyboard, which is why the hover treatment is written as one selector list with it (M1).
Lumino only emits this when a menu bar item's command is disabled; JupyterLab's main menus rarely are.

Emitted only for items whose IMenuItem declares a mnemonic index. Present in the stock main menu, but a deployment that recomposes the menus through overrides.json can drop it — which is exactly the M3 regression this entry is here to catch.
File ▸ New. Also the compound core uses for the disabled-chevron rule this file has to outrank.
The four cells Lumino renders inside a separator row. They are hidden here; if the markup changes shape, core's own ::after border comes back and doubles the line.
The keyboard highlight. If this stops matching, keyboard navigation has gone invisible (R12) — treat a failure here as a release blocker, not a styling nit.
Carries the check glyph and the weight shift that make the toggled state readable without colour (A7, M5).
Core's own compound, repeated verbatim so our reset clears its specificity rather than tying with it.
The application-level current tab — exactly one across every split. This is the hook the accent indicator hangs off.
Core's dirty-tab hack: the close glyph is hidden and this busy circle revealed while the close affordance is not hovered. Deep and fragile by nature — that is why it is asserted.
TabPanel tab bars only appear inside widgets that use one; they share the dock tab treatment so they are styled alongside it.
jp-SideBar-tabIcon does not exist on 4.6.3; the rail glyph is a plain lm-TabBar-tabIcon.

Not styled here — excluded from the webkit rules. Asserted because the exclusion is only correct while core still uses this class for its 4px variant; if the class disappears, the exclusion is dead code and the tiny scrollbars silently grow.
Order matters as much as style here: Dialog renders reject before accept, which is what puts the primary rightmost in LTR without any CSS reordering.
Core paints this as the active-cell bar. It is neutralised here so the inset indicator is the only bar; if the selector stops matching, two bars come back.
The mime type is the hook for the error-output left border. It covers tracebacks and library warnings alike, which is intended.
Kernel selection dialog.
Custom-drawn checkbox styling. No checkbox is rendered at cold boot on 4.6.3 (DirListing ships none by default); they appear in the settings editor and in dialogs.
Some JupyterLab buttons express disabled with aria-disabled rather than the disabled attribute, so both are dimmed.
A <jp-button> custom element. Its control lives in a shadow root and is styled through ::part(control); asserting the host is as deep as querySelectorAll can go.
The plain-DOM path core marks deprecated. Third-party toolbar items still render it, so it is styled; it may legitimately be absent from a stock boot.
The one element exempted from the reduced-motion block. If this class stops matching, the exemption is silently gone and a busy indicator freezes under prefers-reduced-motion (A8).
The `--toolbar-item-gap` rule. `<jp-toolbar>` lays its children out in a shadow root and exposes that variable as the only handle on item spacing, so it is set on the host.

The plate rule. Written with `:where()` on both sides so it weighs exactly what core's own `.jp-Toolbar` weighs and replaces it on source order alone — six upstream rules opt a toolbar OUT of the plate with a single extra class, and an ordinary `body[…]` gate would silently win all six. Measured 18 of 18 toolbars at boot.

The cell toolbar is a FLOATING toolbar rendered against the active cell, so it exists only once a notebook is open AND a cell is active. Measured flaky at 1 run in 3 even with notebook-open driven; optional rather than a break.

The queryable host of the `::part(control)` rule below — a `<jp-button>` whose real control lives in a shadow root. Measured 41 at cold boot; the file browser's two toolbars alone render several. buttons.css records the same host under the stricter `document-open`.
The plain-DOM path core marks deprecated; no shadow root, so the geometry lands on the element itself. Measured 0 in a stock 4.6.3 boot — third-party toolbar items are what still render it.

Inert until TODO P2-12. JupyterLab 4.6.3 has no separator item — the string `jp-Toolbar-separator` does not appear anywhere in the 4.6.3 bundle, JS or CSS — so this rule is the receiving end of the declarative toolbar restructuring that adds the item, not a dependency on markup that exists today.

`Toolbar` adds this the moment its last visible item is removed, and core keeps the plate on it — an empty toolbar still draws a background and a bottom border. Reachable but not reliably: measured 1 on a cold boot (launcher only) and 0 once a notebook is restored, because which toolbars end up empty depends on the layout.

State is `boot`, not `bottom-dock-open`: LabShell constructs the panel at startup and hides it until a widget is added, so the node is in the DOM from a cold start (measured 1). Only the styling waits for `bottom-dock-open`.

The collapse floor. Core caps this bar at 26px and Lumino reads that number back as the area's minimum height, so the floor has to be raised on the BAR — a rule on the area itself is overridden by the inline min-height Lumino writes. Also present from cold start (measured 1).
Measured 0 at boot, 1 with the log console open.

The accent hangs off Lumino's per-tab-bar current tab, not `jp-mod-current` — LabShell only tracks the application-level current tab for the main area, so `jp-mod-current` is never applied down here and core's own accent rule (tabs.css L110, written against `.lm-DockPanel-tabBar`) never matches either.

The bottom dock's resize handle. Lumino renders one handle per child and hides the last, so both exist before the area is ever opened (measured 2 at boot). This file only re-declares the cursor and the hit target; the visible line is drawn once, in tab-bar.css.

surfaces.note: The `:has()` rule is an assertion, not a mechanism: `LabShell._onTabPanelChanged` already hides this panel when its last widget is removed, so in a healthy build it never fires. It is listed as nonQueryable rather than optional because it is only ever true in the failure case it exists to catch.

selectors.note: The MOUNT only. The control inside is a `<jp-search>` whose input lives in a shadow root; restyling it from here would be a fifth bespoke search input (§8.8/S1). The shared `::part()` mapping is P3-12.
The queryable half of the breadcrumb hover rule — the strip washes on hover only when the pointer is NOT over the content itself.
Only emitted for path segments below the root. At the root the strip is a `.jp-BreadCrumbs-home` glyph plus one separator, so this measures 0 on a default boot.
Only while a file is being dragged over a crumb.

A plain text input with no `.jp-mod-styled` class, so inputs.css never sees it — it consumes the `--d4n-input-*` component tokens directly rather than inventing a second text-field spec. In the DOM from boot (measured 1); the widget hides it rather than unmounting it.
Also in the DOM from boot, carrying an inline `display: none` (measured 1).
Populated only while a path is being typed.
Lumino's keyboard highlight on a suggestion. Styled in the same declaration block as `:hover` so arrow-key navigation cannot go invisible (R12).
The sorted column. Core's only signal is `font-weight: 600` on text that is already semibold — invisible — so the foreground moves too (A7). Measured 1 at boot (Name).
Only while a column is being dragged.
One per row. A failure here means the fixture directory is empty, not that the selector moved — check `.jp-DirListing-content:empty` before treating it as an upstream break.
An optional column, off by default in 4.6.3 — the stock header ships Name and Last Modified only, so this measures 0 until the user turns the column on.
Same as `-itemCreated`: an optional column, off by default in 4.6.3.
Needs a click, or a restored selection from a previous session. Carries the tinted plate plus the inset leading accent bar — selection is not colour-only (A7).
Undo #1 of core's selection inversion. Only present once a filter term has been typed.
Core's inverse-colour rule for the same mark on a brand-filled row. Repeated verbatim so our treatment clears it rather than tying with it.
Needs a kernel running on a file in the listed directory. Base of the running-dot rules below.
The inline rename editor — only exists mid-rename.
Drop INTO that directory. Deliberately a different signal from `.jp-mod-native-drop` below, which is a drop into the current directory.
An OS file drag over the listing, i.e. an upload.
The chip that follows the cursor while rows are dragged.

BROKEN AGAINST 4.6.3 — recorded as an assertion, not as a state the harness cannot reach. Measured 0 with the panel open and 19 rows rendered. The class survives only in upstream's own stylesheet (one of its two rules is already marked `@deprecated For backward compatibility when sessions manager does not specify supportsMultipleViews`) and is emitted by nothing in the 4.6.3 bundle: the section list is now a `<jp-tree-view class="jp-TreeView">` inside `.jp-RunningSessions-sectionContainer`. The indent this rule intends therefore lands on `.jp-RunningSessions-sectionContainer > .jp-TreeView` today. Left failing on purpose so the fix happens in running.css rather than being hidden here.

The plain `<div>` the empty-state pseudo-element hangs off. Deliberately not the `<jp-tree-view>` itself: a shadow host's `::after` is subject to slotting and whether it renders at all depends on the component's shadow template.

The queryable half of the `:has(> .jp-TreeView:empty)` empty-state rule, and the element that actually carries the tree indentation in 4.6.3. `.jp-mod-empty` is NOT the hook — measured in 4.6.3, that class is only ever applied inside the searchable-sessions modal, so a rule keyed on it matches nothing and fails silently.

A `<jp-tree-item>`, not an `<li>`. The box a user perceives as the row is `part="positioning-region"` inside its shadow root, so every geometry and surface rule is written against `::part()` — asserting the host is as deep as querySelectorAll can go.

The row whose document is the one in front. Needs a session AND that session's widget focused; measured 0 with the panel open. Core paints the host and then blanks the part, so this rule and its `::part()` twin have to stay a pair.

Rendered only when a section's running item supplies a `detail()` (`h && {h}` in the 4.6.3 bundle). None of the stock sections did in the measured build — 0 of 19 rows — so this is conditional upstream markup rather than a break.
A UUID, read character by character against a log line, which is what the mono ramp is for. Measured 6.

Scoped to `img` on purpose: these are the same server-served kernel rasters the launcher gets and they carry the same dark-mode halo (D-010). The `span` variant is an inline LabIcon that already follows the theme and must NOT gain a plate.
Measured 2 with the panel open, but only sections with nothing to shut down carry it — a fixture where every section is populated has none.

The modal session switcher, a separate mount. Its titles are `<h3>`s rather than accordion titles, which is why the eyebrow treatment is restated for them here — the sidebar's own section headers belong to sidebar.css and are deliberately not touched by this file.
Core's own empty state, already translated — retokened, not replaced.

surfaces.note: The `:focus-within` rule is an accessibility fix, not decoration: the per-row kill button is `visibility: hidden` until the row is hovered, and core's other reveal path keys off `.jp-RunningSessions-item:focus-visible` — the wrong element, because tabbing moves focus to the BUTTON and the item then stops matching. Upstream ends up with a focused, operable, invisible control that shuts down a running kernel (WCAG 2.4.11). It cannot be asserted here, so it is recorded here.

selectors.note: The MOUNT only — margin and width. Same `<jp-search>` the file browser filter uses, left alone for the same reason (S1, P3-12).

The third-party consent notice. Present until the disclaimer is accepted, after which it is gone for that deployment — reachable at a fresh boot but not on a machine where someone has already clicked through.

One of the two sanctioned `!important` sites in this package (§7.4(4)): upstream's own declarations on this class are `!important`, so no amount of specificity reaches them. Core paints BOTH consent buttons red, so the affirmative and the refusal look identical; this restores an ordinary primary/secondary pair.

Core renders these as `<li>`s divided by a hairline. The `border` SHORTHAND is what turns the row into a card AND overwrites that divider in one declaration — four `border-*` longhands would leave core's bottom line 1px inside our own.
Only entries whose package declares a homepage — measured 1 of 9.

`ListEntry` guards this on `performAction` (`e.performAction&&h.createElement("div",{className:"jp-extensionmanager-entry-buttons"}…` in the 4.6.3 bundle), which the panel withholds until the third-party disclaimer is accepted. Measured 0 of 9 entries pre-acceptance.
Guarded on `i.approved` — only when the deployment's package index marks the extension approved.

One of the four entry states core does express as a class. "Installed vs enabled vs disabled" is NOT one of them in 4.6 — it is carried entirely by which buttons the entry renders — so there is no selector to hang a treatment on.
Only when a search returns more than one page — measured 0 in an air-gapped container.
The host is always rendered (measured 1); only the `.jp-mod-hasPending` state below is conditional.
Only while an install or uninstall is in flight. The indeterminate bar itself is core's animation — reduced-motion is already handled in motion.css and reaches it.

The state users hit most: this panel needs network access to a package index and an air-gapped deployment never gets it. Not reachable from a scripted boot only because whether it fires depends on the container's egress.

Core's own translated "No entries" — retokened and centred rather than replaced from CSS, which would drop the translation. Present only for a section with no results; measured 1 in an air-gapped container where the Discover section cannot fetch, and 0 in a networked one.
The uninstall confirmation dialog.

surfaces.note: `a:visited` is listed as nonQueryable rather than optional because querySelectorAll never reports a match for it — browsers evaluate `:visited` as unvisited outside of painting, for history-privacy reasons — so an assertion on it could only ever fail.

importOrder.why: `.lm-CommandPalette-input` is styled by both files at identical (0,2,1) specificity and both declare padding — inputs.css sets the `padding` shorthand for the §8.8 base input, this file restates `padding-right` to clear the search glyph. A tie on specificity is resolved by source order, so if style/index.css ever imports this file BEFORE inputs.css the glyph clearance is silently lost. The alternative was an `!important`, which §7.4(4) reserves for beating upstream `!important` only.

selectors.note: `top` is pinned to `--d4n-top-panel-height` rather than core's bare 38px so the palette hangs off the bottom edge of the chrome; the two are the same number today only by coincidence.

Stripped back to a positioning context. Every declaration on it removes something core draws — a 30px height that fights the base input's 28px, a second background, an inset box-shadow that reads as a second outline, a 9px side inset, and an `overflow: overlay` that clips the input's focus ring.

Core's focus treatment, neutralised: the input's own `:focus` styling plus the ring from focus.css already cover it, and leaving both produces a ring inside a ring. Measured 1 — the modal palette focuses its input on open.

See importOrder above. `float: none` is load-bearing: core's `float: left` takes the input out of flow, so the wrapper collapses and the glyph lands in the wrong place once the wrapper is no longer a fixed 30px box.

Lumino's KEYBOARD highlight on a category header — not `:hover` and not `:focus`. Written in the same declaration block as the hover so the two cannot drift apart (M1, R12). Measured 0 on open; it needs arrow-key navigation the harness does not drive.
Needs a typed query — measured 0 on open, 18 after two keystrokes.

The row Enter will run — the palette's selection, moved by arrow keys and not by the pointer, which is why it is deliberately STRONGER than hover. Lumino leaves activeIndex at -1 until a query is typed or an arrow key is pressed: measured 0 on open, 1 after typing.
Measured 134 of 238 rows on a stock boot — most commands need a document.

Needs a typed query. Weight-led rather than tinted: after two keystrokes every visible row carries a mark, and a tint repeated down the whole list is stripe noise that also collides with the selected row's plate (A7).
Core's inverse-colour rule for a mark on a brand-filled active row, repeated so our treatment clears it.

`:empty` is structural, so it IS queryable — this one is asserted rather than filed under nonQueryable. Not defensive tidying either: Lumino renders the element on EVERY row whether or not the command has a binding, and measured 160 of 238 were empty. Without the rule most rows carry a 2px bordered box floating at their right edge.

Needs a query that matches nothing — measured 1 with a nonsense query. This is the LIVE no-results hook; apputils' own `.lm-CommandPalette-content:empty::after { content: 'No results' }` is dead, because Lumino 2.9's `renderEmptyMessage` always appends this `<li>` so the content element is never `:empty` (measured 0 for `.lm-CommandPalette-content:empty` in that same state). Styling the dead one would have looked correct in review and shipped a state nobody would ever see — which is the failure mode this manifest exists to catch — so it is deliberately not styled and deliberately not recorded as a dependency.
The entry separator. Measured 3 in a freshly-opened console.

The prompt gutter. The level never appears as text in the DOM — `LogConsoleOutputPrompt` writes it to `node.dataset.logLevel` and nothing else — so the attribute IS the hook. The theme gate plus the attribute puts this at (0,4,1), which beats core's own (0,3,0) per-level rules without `!important`. `flex: 0 0 auto` has to be restated alongside `width`: the log console substitutes a bare `Widget` for the usual `OutputPrompt`, so the node never picks up `.jp-OutputPrompt`'s `flex` and its default `flex-shrink: 1` would let a long line squeeze the chip.

A SIXTH value the public `LogLevel` union does not mention — it is `Private.LogLevel` index 5 — but it does reach the DOM: `Logger` writes it on the entries the console generates about itself ("Log level set to …", and the `<hr/>` from Add Checkpoint). Measured as the ONLY level present in a freshly-opened console (3 of 3 prompts). Asserted here precisely because an upstream tidy-up could remove it, which would silently strip the `content: none` that keeps a sixth colour out of a ramp of five.

The timestamp. `LogConsoleOutputPrompt` appends it as a bare, class-less `<div>`, so the child combinator is the only handle there is — and it is exact, because the prompt has no other child. If a class ever appears here, this entry is what notices.

Two distinct states share this node — "No source selected." and "No log messages." — and core supplies both strings, translated. In the DOM whenever the panel is open, messages or not (measured 1 alongside 3 entries).

An `HTMLSelect` in `jp-DefaultStyle` — a different control from the `select.jp-mod-styled` inputs.css owns, so the two do not overlap. Not a source picker: it sets the minimum level the current source records.
Only while no source is selected — measured 1 with an empty dock and 0 with a notebook in front.
The "N messages" indicator in the status bar.

Transient. `LogConsoleStatus` adds `jp-mod-highlighted` and `jp-LogConsoleStatusItem` at construction; `jp-mod-selected` is added only by `_showHighlighted()` on a flash — a new message at or above the flash level arriving while the console is hidden — and removed by `_clearHighlight()`. Measured 0 with the console open, which is the resting case.

Inherits the transient parent above. The descendant is from @jupyterlab/statusbar, not logconsole — core hardcodes `color: white` on it (its own comment admits it is a contrast patch); both ends become tokens here.

surfaces.note: The five chip rules re-express the level as a filled badge with the name in it, which is what turns the level colour from an 11px text target (1.4.3, 4.5:1 — unmeetable) into a non-text contrast target (1.4.11, 3:1), and stops severity being carried by colour alone (1.4.1). They cannot be asserted — generated content is not in the DOM — so the queryable prompts above are what guards them: if `[data-log-level]` stops matching, every chip goes with it.

PRD 6.5 inventories toasts as .jp-Notification-*. Those names reach only the STATUS BAR item; the popup itself is rendered by react-toastify and carries Toastify__* classes. Styling the documented names alone leaves the popup unthemed.

Styled as T2 rather than the T3 replacement PRD 8.5.1 specifies -- four of its four justifications are reachable from CSS on 4.6.3. See docs/decisions.md D-015. The jp-mod-highlighted entry below is the load-bearing one: it is CORE's marker for an interactive item, and the whole passive/interactive split keys off it, so if upstream drops it this job is what tells us.

selectors.note: Core marks every interactive item with this. The passive/interactive distinction in status-bar.css depends on it entirely.
Opens only when a hover item (kernel picker, running sessions) is clicked.

surfaces.note: Presentation half of PRD 8.11. The behavioural half (fixed section order, root-directory copy, no-kernels error state, >12-kernel search) is TODO P2-15; see docs/decisions.md D-016. Note .jp-Launcher-cwd EXISTS on 4.6 -- 8.11.4 calls the readout net-new, which is wrong; only the empty-path root case is missing.

selectors.note: Kernel cards only -- the raster kernelIconUrl the neutral plate exists for (D-010).
LabIcon mounts its svg inside a wrapper div, not as a direct child.
